question: A cone is sliced into two sections by a plane that is parallel to its base, with the upper section representing 1/8 of the overall volume. What is the ratio of the heights of the smaller cone to the original cone?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

When a cone is sliced parallel to its base, the smaller cone formed is similar to the original cone.

For similar 3D figures, Height Ratio = ∛(Volume Ratio)

Given Volume Ratio = 1 : 8

⇒ Height Ratio = ∛(1/8) = 1/2

**∴ The correct answer is 1 : 2.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Volume of the upper section (smaller cone), V₁ = 1/8 × Volume of the original cone (V₂)

**Formula Used:**

Volume of a cone, V = 1/3 × π × r² × h
